pr_title: Fix issues related to JsonSerializerOptions mutation and caching.
pr_body:
Supersedes #65799. After conversation with @layomia in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/65799#discussion_r813409685 I realized that the caching implementation introduced in #64646 contains a bug. More specifically, a locked/immutable `JsonSerializerOptions` instance can still be mutated by the serialization infrastructure in couple of important ways:

* [Setting the `JsonSerializerContext` field](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/b3465af11d9bc77ef3fa43cee744adf3ec7c3665/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Serialization/JsonSerializerContext.cs#L106).
* [Materializing the `_typeInfoCreationFunc` field](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/b3465af11d9bc77ef3fa43cee744adf3ec7c3665/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Serialization/JsonSerializerOptions.cs#L592) if the options instance has been passed to a reflection serialization API.

Both of these changes alter the `JsonTypeInfo` resolution semantics in important ways, and as such they can invalidate the current contents of the metadata cache. This PR makes the following changes:

* `JsonSerializerContext` values can now only be attached to _mutable_ `JsonSerializerOptions` instances. This is a potential breaking change, however the new throwing behavior is arguably better than the current one (nondeterministic use of serialization metadata).
* Make `IsInitializedForReflectionSerializer` an instance method instead of a static, and ensure it gets propagated correctly to shared caching contexts.
* Fix #65770.

I ran the benchmark suite and no performance regressions were recorded.

I'm removing the breaking-change label since in hindsight, the removed behavior (i.e. ability to add a `JsonSerializerContext` to a locked `JsonSerializerOptions` instance) is fairly pathological (generally resulting in nondeterministic contract resolution in .NET 6) so it probably doesn't warrant mention in the documentation.

issue_context.title: Repeatedly initialize the static variables s_defaultSimpleConverters and s_defaultFactoryConverters when calling the method GetConverter of JsonSerializerOptions
issue_context.body:
### Description

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/a1a653c7217706fcb820914d65126234bc2447a8/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Serialization/JsonSerializerOptions.Converters.cs#L162

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/a1a653c7217706fcb820914d65126234bc2447a8/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/src/System/Text/Json/Serialization/JsonSerializerOptions.Converters.cs#L27

### Reproduction Steps

According to the referenced code

### Expected behavior

Variables s_defaultSimpleConverters and s_defaultFactoryConverters are initialized only once

### Actual behavior

Variables s_defaultSimpleConverters and s_defaultFactoryConverters are repeatedly initialized with each call

Good catch, thanks. It should be possible to fix the issue by adding a null check in the RootBuiltInConverters method. Would you be interested in contributing a PR?

Seems to be introduced in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/57327/files#r688365200
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/523221/155324319-052e88b1-186b-4b89-9802-ba7612b6cc13.png)

(screenshot, because github links for PR's parts are terrible)

review_comments: I'm not sure if this is under lock or not, but if not would it make sense to check for `s_typeInfoCreationFunc` being null instead? if you check for the first field this might backfire once in a while if first thread starts initializing while other one assumes it's already initialized because first field is set
It's ok for contending threads to initialize these fields multiple times, this is a check meant to avoid incurring additional allocations once initialization has completed.
Should the same asserted for when a source-gen overload is used?
Should we `Debug.Assert` that the related static properties are also `null`?
